brief: Top-down view through still water onto pale turquoise mosaic tiles, a child's tangerine-orange swim goggles resting slightly off-centre with a strap curling toward the corner. Over everything sits a trembling net of caustic light, bright wobbling cells drawn in fine, slightly broken white and pale lemon pen lines that bend across grout seams and wrap over the goggles' domed lenses. Beneath them, layered transparent watercolour glazes of cerulean, viridian and pale aqua build the tile colour, with soft-edged bands where the light thins. The goggles carry crisp specular glints and a faint warped shadow. The effect is cool, shimmering and photographically exact.

A split jackfruit rendered with obsessive realism: waxy saffron bulbs, sticky white latex threads, a nubbled green rind. It sits enthroned inside an arched Tanjore-style niche of raised gold. The surrounding field is dense opaque colour in vermilion, emerald and deep lapis, edged with thick, confident dark outlines. Clusters of round "gem" dots in ruby and jade stud the arch, each with a hard white catchlight so they read as glass cabochons. Pen and marker work is heavy and enamel-like. The fruit alone receives soft, modelled shading, so the photographic jackfruit sits inside a flat, gleaming devotional frame.

A raw egg frozen at the instant it bursts against a corrugated galvanised wall, and the whole picture behaves like an action painting. Flung spray, airborne droplets and splattered streaks of albumen explode outward, but the yolk, the shell shards and the zinc ripples are hyperreal: wet gloss, membrane wrinkles, a crisp crack along each shard edge. Violent marker swipes and spatter carry the motion. The palette is cadmium yolk yellow, translucent egg-white greys, cold steel and one rusty seam. The energy is explosive and the detail forensic.

A dropped wedge of watermelon lies on cracked charcoal asphalt under brutal overhead noon sun. The only shadow is a tight black sliver tucked directly beneath it. The colours are blown and saturated: flat marker reds, acid green rind, glare-white highlights where the light bleaches the wet flesh, glossy black seeds. The asphalt is gritty, built from dry-marker scumbling and stippled aggregate, with faint heat shimmer. Nothing has form-shadow, so everything reads flattened and stark. It is cropped low and wide, with the slice placed in the lower third.

Strings of peeled persimmons drying under the eave of a farmhouse. Their wrinkled, sugar-bloomed skins are rendered in obsessive hyperreal detail, yet the whole is printed in the manner of a self-carved woodblock. Flat, slightly uneven watercolour layers stand in for each block: burnt orange, persimmon red, smoky indigo shadow and a sienna eave. Pale pencil woodgrain texture shows through every fill, as if the block's grain printed along with the ink. Registration is slightly off, so thin paper-white gaps appear at the edges. The light is cold autumn sun from the side. The fruit hang in a staggered vertical rhythm across a buff ground.

Seen from overhead, thousands of hyperreal rice grains are spilled across a dark, cracked dung-and-mud floor in umber and burnt sienna. The grains have fallen into a loose spiral ring that echoes a Warli circle dance, with a few clustered triangular piles like figures. Each grain is drawn individually in chalky white and pale cream pencil, with a translucent tip and a tiny shadow. The floor is layered dry-brush watercolour with granulation and hairline cracks. The palette is restricted to earth browns and white. The rhythm is ritual and repetitive, while every grain stays exact.

A tall glass of iced coffee seen from the side at eye level, a moment after the cream was poured. Inside, a horizontal shear line curls into a row of breaking, rolling waves where pale cream meets dark espresso, exactly like Kelvin–Helmholtz billow clouds. Wet-on-wet watercolour bleeds raw umber into ivory along the crests, and fine spray mists the turbulent edges. Ice cubes refract the waves, and condensation beads on the glass carry pinpoint highlights. The background is a soft unfocused wash of warm grey. The mood is calm, suspended and precise.

A mandarin orange dismantled in mid-air in the manner of an exploded-view diagram. The peel hovers as a split shell, the pith web floats free, and the segments fan outward in ordered isometric sequence with a single seed beside them. Every part is rendered in hyperreal coloured-pencil realism: glistening pulp vesicles, a pocked, oily rind, fibrous white strands. Thin, ruled graphite leader lines and dashed axis lines connect each part back to its origin, with small blank callout circles. The ground is warm grey drafting vellum with faint construction lines left visible.

A small wooden fishing skiff hauled up on grey shingle, shrouded in patched tarpaulins. Faded indigo, washed denim blue, sky blue and one rust-orange square are lashed and stitched over one another like boro mending. Layered watercolour fills overlap at irregular edges, with dry-brush fraying, sun-bleached creases and salt stains. Visible pen-drawn running stitches, knotted ropes and grommets hold the layers together. The light is an overcast flat grey with soft shadows, the view is three-quarter at low height, and the boat fills most of the frame.

An extreme close-up of a woman's cheek and closed eye under a drying clay face mask. The grey-ochre clay has split into a fine polygonal craquelure like drought-baked earth, and smooth, pore-detailed living skin shows through the cracks. Soft charcoal mass builds the parched clay plates, and crisp sepia ink draws the crack network, with curled lifting edges casting tiny shadows. The skin is rendered in warm, glowing watercolour glazes. Raking light from one side emphasises the relief, and the palette is umber, bone, dusty ochre and flushed rose.

A raw squid lying on a glossy white enamel tray, painted only in cobalt blue on white like underglaze porcelain. Its chromatophore speckles, the translucent mantle and the curling tentacles with their suckers are all built from graded cobalt washes, from pale wash-blue to dense pooled navy at the edges. Fine blue pen lines describe the suckers and fins. A wet glassy sheen comes from untouched white highlights and a faint pooled-water reflection. There is no other colour anywhere. The composition is diagonal and cropped, cool and immaculate.

Thin citrus slices are arranged in a perfect circle on a flat grey board, ordered like a colour-theory hue wheel. The sequence runs lime, Key lime, lemon, Meyer, navel, tangerine, blood orange, pink grapefruit and Cara Cara, with complementary pairs facing each other across the ring. Backlit from below, each slice glows translucent with individual juice vesicles, membranes and seeds. Transparent watercolour glazes are layered to keep that luminosity, with tiny ruled pencil annotations at the edges like a didactic chart. The look is clean, diagrammatic and mouth-watering.

A frame-filling bookshelf of worn paperback spines, each one a narrow vertical strip with its own blocks and bands of colour. Their offset heights and staggered stripes evoke kente strips stitched side by side. The palette is kente gold, emerald, crimson, black and a little indigo. Everything is rendered in dense, burnished coloured pencil with creased spine cracks, sun-faded tops, frayed laminate and tiny stickers. The spines carry no readable text, only abstract rectangles of colour. Each strip has its own subtle shading, so the whole surface reads as woven yet utterly photographic.

A spare, asymmetric kitchen still life composed on ikebana's three-line principle. A tall leek leans skyward, a steel ladle angles mid-height, and a single red rubber band rests low. All three are anchored in a chrome dish rack set far to the left, with a vast quiet field of pale celadon-grey wall. Fine graphite drawing is glazed with thin, exact watercolour: the leek's bluish bloom and soil-flecked roots, the ladle's warped reflections. Edges are razor-clean and the negative space is deliberate, so the arrangement feels balanced.

A close hyperreal portrait of a white cow's face: wet pink nostrils, long eyelashes, a velvety hide with faint grey mottling, and a marigold garland slung beneath the jaw. It is framed in the lyrical Pahari miniature manner, with a flat jade-green ground, a slender saffron-and-crimson inner border, and a broad salmon outer margin scattered with tiny floral sprigs. Fine watercolour stippling and hair-thin pencil lines build the fur strand by strand. The light is soft, even and devotional, and the painting is small-scale and jewel-like.

A tight crop of an unmade bed with rumpled cotton sheets printed in madder-red toile de Jouy: shepherds, ruined arches and leafy trees. The pastoral scenes ripple, compress and vanish into deep folds. Fine engraved-style pen hatching in a single madder red on warm cream renders both the print and the sheet's form. Folds are shaded by denser crosshatching, so the realism of the cloth comes entirely through the toile's own line language. A dented pillow edge intrudes at the top. The feeling is intimate, quiet and morning-soft.

A slab of cultured butter sits on a scarred oak board, with a knife curl lifted from one corner. The whole image is built like layered wax: thick, translucent glazes in buttercup, cream and honey, fused into a soft luminous skin. Scraped back in places, these glazes reveal underlayers. The butter shows faint knife striations, a cold-condensation bloom and a ragged cut edge. The board grain is incised with fine scratched lines. A dim, warm window light from behind gives the fat an inner translucency.

A square of lasagne lifted from the dish and seen exactly side-on, its cut face filling a wide horizontal frame like a geologist's section. Pasta sheets, ricotta seams, bolognese bands and a browned cheese crust stack as clean strata, with oozing intrusions and bubbled voids. The medium is dense coloured pencil, burnished in sienna, cadmium red, ivory and caramel. Small inked tick marks and hatched legend swatches sit in the margin, without words. A steam-fogged background fades upward into blank paper.

A halved ripe fig rendered entirely in rigid horizontal rows of round ink dots, like an impact printer's output. Dot density builds the seed-packed garnet flesh, the cream pith and the bruised aubergine skin with startling realism. The paper is continuous tractor-feed stock with pale mint-green bands and perforated sprocket margins down both sides. Occasional rows double-strike darker, and a faint ribbon-fade stripe crosses the fruit. The only colour is ribbon black plus a single overprinted pass of magenta-red dots in the flesh.

A tight, tilted crop of a bare thigh just lifted from a rattan chair. The woven pattern is pressed into the skin as pink ridges and pale hollows, and the real chair weave runs off the lower edge. The medium is sepia and raw-umber watercolour glazes worked into graphite. Each cane strand is drawn with its glossy node, split fibre and frayed binding. The skin carries faint vellus hair and pressure blanching, with rose madder pooling in the dents. Light is soft afternoon from one side. The whole picture is a quiet over-and-under rhythm with no background, only weave and flesh.
